The precise and continuous measurement of structural displacement is an imperative component of Structural Health Monitoring (SHM). Displacement time histories serve as the most direct physical indicator of a structure's global deformation, stiffness degradation, and behavioral response to operational and extreme environmental loads1.

The continuous assessment and condition monitoring of civil, mechanical, and aerospace infrastructure rely heavily on the accurate extraction of dynamic characteristics, a process fundamentally governed by Operational Modal Analysis (OMA). Traditional Experimental Modal Analysis (EMA) requires measured and controlled artificial excitation, such as impulse hammers or electromagnetic shakers.

The central finding is negative but methodologically important: **among the recent structural-vision papers screened, I found no study that verifiably preregistered a three-way comparison of raw vision output, a causal Kalman filter, and a non-causal Rauch–Tung–Striebel smoother before inspecting test ground truth**. There is also no matched benchmark in which the same vision front end, state model, covariance-estimation rule, sensor inputs, and test sequences are held fixed while only the estimator is changed among those three choices.

This review finds a **small but technically important direct literature** in which Frequency Domain Decomposition or covariance-driven Stochastic Subspace Identification is applied to displacement time histories extracted from cameras. The evidence base is much narrower than the broader vision-based vibration literature, which is dominated by Fourier peak picking, motion magnification, blind source separation, NExT–ERA, and image-processing validation studies.

Step 00 — ROS Bag Audit
=======================
Purpose:  Extract and report metadata from a single ROS 1 bag file. Inputs:   Path to a .bag file (--bag argument)
Outputs:  Terminal summary + results/step00/<bag_name>_audit.json
Accepts:  FPS 59-61 Hz per camera topic, no frame gap > 0.1 s

Step 01 — Frame Export
======================
Purpose:  Extract PNG frames and timestamps from a ROS 1 bag file. Inputs:   Path to a .bag file (--bag argument) or --all flag for all WTT bags.

Step 02 — AprilTag Detection
=============================
Purpose:  Detect AprilTag corners in exported PNG frames. Inputs:   results/step01/{condition}/{cam}/frame_XXXXXX.png
          results/step01/{condition}/{cam}/timestamps.csv
          config/pipeline_config.yaml
Outputs:  results/step02/{condition}/{cam}/detections.csv
          results/step02/{condition}/{cam}/summary.json
Schema (detections.csv):
    frame_idx       int     — links back to step01 PNG and timestamps.csv
    tag_id          int     — AprilTag ID (all cameras see tag_id=0)
    cx, cy          float   — pixel centroid
    c0x,c0y ..

Step 03 — Quality Scoring
==========================
Purpose:  Compute per-frame quality scores for AprilTag detections. Enriches step02 detections.csv with quality metrics.

Step 04 — Pose Estimation (World-Frame Transform)
==================================================
Purpose:  Estimate 6-DOF pose of the AprilTag in each frame using solvePnP. Produces per-frame translation (x, y, z) and quaternion rotation
          in the camera's own coordinate frame.

Step 05 — Cross-Camera Synchronization
=======================================
Purpose:  Resample all three cameras onto a common 60 Hz time grid so that
          downstream steps can compare per-timestep values across cameras. The cameras were started sequentially (not hardware-triggered).

Step 06 — Baseline-Aligned Fusion
===================================
Purpose:  Remove per-camera DC offset (full-run mean) to convert absolute
          camera-frame positions into relative displacements. Compute the
          aligned inter-camera Z disagreement as a key publishable result.

Step 07 — Motion Decomposition
================================
Purpose:  Decompose aligned per-camera displacements into two physically
          meaningful channels:

          bending_avg_y_mm  = ((cam1_y + cam2_y) / 2 + cam3_y) / 2   [cross-bridge average]
              — Full-model average vertical displacement across all three markers. Represents bridge bending (vertical oscillation).

Step 08 — Frequency Analysis
==============================
Purpose:  Compute PSD and dominant frequency for bending and torsion proxy
          channels across all conditions. Reports dominant peak and nearest
          structural reference bin as SEPARATE fields — never conflated.

Fiducial marker-based vision displacement measurement for structural health monitoring reached a practical but still condition-sensitive state of the art from 2020 to 2026. Across this period, AprilTag- and ArUco-based systems repeatedly achieved subpixel tracking and, in several laboratory and some field configurations, converted that into sub-millimetre displacement accuracy, especially when camera geometry was calibrated, targets were well resolved, and line of sight remained stable  (Shajihan et al., 2022; Li et al., 2024; Ajmal et al., 2026).

Yes, **synchronized cameras measure** **aeroelastic response** in wind tunnels, with strong evidence across 2D, 3D, and full-field setups.: **Figure 1:** Research consensus on camera-based aeroelastic wind tunnel measurement

The directly relevant studies are few. In this corpus, the clearest wind-tunnel or aeroelastic model validations of **vision-based displacement** against a **laser displacement sensor or LDV** are tall-building aeroelastic model studies by Huang and colleagues and a wind-tunnel motion-capture study by Park et al.; bridge-deck sectional-model papers in this set mainly use laser sensors themselves rather than validating a vision system against them.

Multi-camera timing synchronization for structural health monitoring and vibration measurement has been achieved with both **hardware-triggered** and **software/offline post-processing** methods, but the smallest reported residual timing uncertainties come from hardware or timestamp-based schemes in the **tens of microseconds**, while software-only camera alignment more often reports **millisecond-level** residual offsets. Wind-tunnel and aeroelastic applications do exist, but they are still sparse and usually emphasize feasibility or agreement with reference sensors more than explicit residual timing-error budgets  (Wang et al., 2026; Ajmal et al., 2026; Le et al., 2023; Hsu et al., 2024).

Yes, **vision-based tracking** generally **matched reference sensors**, but direct **LDV wind-tunnel** evidence is sparse.: **Figure 1:** Research consensus on vision tracking agreement with reference sensors

Optical-flow-based and digital-image-correlation-based structural displacement methods published from 2020–2026 are accurate in many laboratory and some field settings, but both families show recurring accuracy limitations under dynamic, long-duration, or environmentally difficult conditions. Optical flow most consistently struggles with cumulative drift, frame-update drift, limited large-motion range in classical formulations, illumination sensitivity, and low-amplitude noise sensitivity  (Gao et al., 2023; Peng et al., 2024; Chen et al., 2024; Kahya, 2026).

Synchronized camera systems have been used to measure aeroelastic deformation, displacement, vibration, modal response, flutter-related motion, and coupled fluid–structure behavior in wind tunnels from low-speed civil tests to transonic and supersonic aerospace experiments. The strongest evidence comes from long-running videogrammetry and stereo/DIC studies that directly validated camera-based measurements against lasers, accelerometers, strain gauges, simulations, or pressure/flow diagnostics  (Burner & Liu, 2001; Brouwer et al., 2023; Najafi & Paulsen, 2017).

Direct bridge and aeroelastic vision-validation studies in this set mostly report **RMSE or NRMSE**, while explicit **correlation coefficients** are rarely stated. The clearest numerical bridge results come from field or lab bridge studies, whereas the wind-tunnel aeroelastic papers usually claim agreement with laser sensors without giving correlation or RMSE in the indexed text  (Marendić et al., 2026; Zhu et al., 2025; Huang et al., 2018).
